If riches increase, set not thine heart upon them. Ps. 62:10.

Introduction

He was 87 years old, and felt himself (as he himself wrote) as one “with dim eyes, shaking hands, and tottering feet.” But he had a message to give yet. With a vehemence that seems even greater than his normal fervency, John Wesley warned of a great danger to his people—riches. From a small handful, his movement had grown to 135,000 members with over 500 itinerant preachers. His preaching was effective in noticeably changing the moral and ethical climate of England, to the point that he is credited with saving England from a bloodbath like later happened in the French Revolution. But a sinister evil lurked among his people, and Wesley used some of his last remaining strength to call this evil for what it was.

May we who are many times richer than the people of John Wesley’s day have ears to hear.

(Note that some of Wesley’s English has been updated and that the subtitles are not original. The signature under the title is a facsimile of his own signature.)

From that express declaration of our Lord, “It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven,” we may easily learn that none can have riches without being greatly endangered by them. But if the danger of barely having them is so great, how much greater is the danger of increasing them! This danger is great even to those who receive what is transmitted to them by their forefathers; but it is abundantly greater to those who acquire them by their skill and industry. Therefore, nothing can be more prudent than this caution: “If riches increase, set not thine heart upon them.” Ps. 62:10

It is true, riches, and the increase of them, are the gift of God. Yet great care is to be taken that what is intended for a blessing does not turn into a curse. To prevent this, it is highly expedient to consider seriously:

  1. What is meant by riches; and when they may be said to increase.
  2. What is implied in setting our hearts upon them; and how we may avoid it.

What does “riches” mean?

Consider, first, what is here meant by riches. Indeed some may imagine that it is hardly possible to mistake the meaning of this common word. Yet, in truth, there are thousands in this mistake; and many of them quite innocently. A person of note, hearing a sermon preached upon this subject several years ago, between surprise and indignation broke out aloud, “Why does he talk about riches here? There is no rich man at Whitehaven, except Sir James L----r.”

And it is true there was none but he that had £40,0001 a year, and some millions in ready money. But a man may be rich that has not £100 a year, nor even £1000 in cash. Whosoever has food to eat, and raiment to put on, with something over, is rich. Whoever has the necessaries and conveniences of life for himself and his family, and a little to spare for them that have not, is properly a rich man; unless he is a miser, a lover of money, one that hoards up what he can and ought to give to the poor. For if so, he is a poor man still, though he has millions in the bank; yea, he is the poorest of men; for:

The beggars but a common lot deplore;
The rich poor man’s emphatically poor.

Beware of judging

But here an exception may be made. A person may have more than necessaries and conveniences for his family, and yet not be rich. For he may be in debt; and his debts may amount to more than he is worth. But if this be the case, he is not a rich man, how much money soever he has in his hands. Yea, a man of business may be afraid that this is the real condition of his affairs, whether it be or no; and then he cannot be so charitable as he would, for fear of being unjust. How many that are engaged in trade are in this very condition! Those especially that trade to a very large amount; for their affairs are frequently so entangled that it is not possible to determine, with any exactness, how much they are worth, or, indeed, whether they are worth anything or nothing. Should we not make a fair allowance for them?

And beware of forming a hasty judgment concerning the fortune of others. There may be secrets in the situation of a person, which few but God are acquainted with. Some years ago, I told a gentleman, “Sir, I am afraid you are covetous.”

He asked me, “What is the reason of your fear?”

I answered, “A year ago, when I made a collection for the expense of repairing the Foundery, you subscribed five guineas. At the subscription made this year you subscribed only half a guinea.”

He made no reply; but after a time asked, “Pray, sir, answer me a question: Why do you live upon potatoes?” (I did so between three and four years.)

I replied, “It has much conduced to my health.”

He answered, “I believe it has. But did you not do it likewise to save money?”

I said, “I did; for what I save from my own food expense will feed another that else would have none.”

“But, sir,” said he, “if this be your motive you may save much more. I know a man that goes to the market at the beginning of every week: There he buys a pennyworth of parsnips, which he boils in a large quantity of water. The parsnips serve him for food, and the water for drink the whole following week. So his meat and drink together cost him only a penny a week.”

This he constantly did, though he earned then £200/year,2 so that he could pay the debts which he had contracted before he knew God! And this was he, whom I had set down for a covetous man!

What about you?

But there are those who are conscious before God that they are rich. And, doubtless, some among you are of the number. You have more of the goods of this world than is needful either for yourself or your family. Let each consider for himself. Do your riches increase? Do not you understand that plain expression? Have you not more money, or more of money’s worth, than you had 10 or 20 years ago, or at this time last year? If you keep any account, you can easily know this. Indeed you ought to know; otherwise, you are not a good steward, even in this respect, of the mammon of unrighteousness. And every man, whether engaged in trade or not, ought to know whether his substance lessens or increases.

But many have found out a way never to be rich, though their substance increase ever so much. It is this: As fast as money comes in they invest it, either in land or enlarging their business. By this means each of these, by keeping his cash assets low, can still say, “I am not rich.” He can say that even though he has 10, 20, or 100 times more substance than he had some years ago.

This may be explained by a recent case: A gentleman came to a merchant in London a few years ago and told him, “Sir, I beg you will give me a guinea3 for a worthy family that is in great distress.”

He replied, “Really, Mr. M., I cannot well afford to give you it just now; but if you will call upon me when I am worth £10,000, then I will give you ten guineas.”

Mr. M., after some time, called upon him again and said, “Sir, I claim your promise; now you are worth £10,000.”

He replied, “That is very true: But I assure you, I cannot spare one guinea so well as I could then.”

It is possible for a man to cheat himself by this ingenious device. And he may cheat other men; for as long “as you doest good unto yourself, men will speak well of thee.” “A right good man,” says the Londoner, “he is worth a plum” (£100,000). But, alas! he cannot deceive God; and he cannot deceive the devil. Ah, no! The curse of God is upon thee already, and on all that you have. And tomorrow, when the devil seizes your soul, will he not say, “What do all your riches profit you?” Will they purchase a pillow for your head, in the lake of fire burning with brimstone? Or will they procure you a cup of “water to cool your tongue,” while you are tormented in that flame?” O follow the wise direction here given so that God may not say unto thee, “Thou fool!”

This mental gymnastics, therefore, will not avail. It will not be any protection either against the wrath of God or the malice and power of the devil. You are convicted already of “setting thy heart” upon your riches, if you reinvest all you have above the conveniences of life, on adding money to money, house to house, or field to field, without giving at least a tenth of your income (the Jewish proportion) to the poor. By whatsoever means your riches increase, whether with or without labour; whether by trade, inheritances, or any other way; unless your charities increase in the same proportion; unless you give a full tenth of your substance, of your fixed and occasional income; you undoubtedly set your heart upon your gold, and it will “eat thy flesh as fire!”4

The hardheartedness of the covetousness

But O! who can convince a rich man that he sets his heart upon riches? For considerably above half a century I have spoken on this head, with all the plainness that was in my power. But with how little effect! I doubt whether I have, in all that time, convinced fifty misers of covetousness. When the lover of money was described ever so clearly, and painted in the strongest colors, who applied it to himself? To whom did God, and all that knew him, say, “Thou art the man!” If He speaks to any of you that are present, O do not stop your ears! Rather say, with Zaccheus, “Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have done any wrong to any man, I restore fourfold.” He did not mean that he had done this in time past; but that he determined to do so for the time to come. I charge thee before God, you lover of money, to “go and do likewise!”

I have a message from God unto thee, O rich man! whether you wilt hear, or whether you wilt forbear. Riches have increased with thee; at the peril of your soul, “set not thine heart upon them!” Be thankful to Him that gave thee such a talent, so much power of doing good. Yet dare not to rejoice over them, but with fear and trembling, “Beware you cleave not unto them, lest you be entangled and perish.” Do not make them your end, your chief delight, your happiness, your god! See that you expect not happiness in money, nor anything that is purchasable thereby; in gratifying either the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, or the pride of life.

But let us descend to particulars; and see that each of you deal faithfully with his own soul. If any of you have now twice, thrice, or four times as much substance as when you first saw my face, faithfully examine yourselves and see if you do not set your hearts, if not directly on money or riches themselves, yet on some of the things that are purchasable thereby; which comes to the same thing. All those the Apostle John includes under that general name, the world; and the desire of them, or to seek happiness in them, under that form, “the love of the world.”

Defining “the world”

This he divides into three branches, “the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the pride of life.” Fairly examine yourselves with regard to these.

  • First, as to “the desire of the flesh.” I believe this means the seeking of happiness in the things that gratify the senses. To instance in one: Do not you seek your happiness in enlarging the pleasure of tasting? To be more particular: Do you not eat more plentifully, or more delicately, than you did ten or twenty years ago? Do not you use more drink, or drink of a more costly kind, than you did then? Do you sleep on as hard a bed as you did once, supposing your health will bear it? To touch on one point more: do you fast as often, now that you are rich, as you did when you were poor? Ought you not, in all reason, to do this rather more often than more seldom? I am afraid your own heart condemns you. You are not clear in this matter.
  • The second branch of the love of the world, “the desire of the eyes,” is of a wider extent. We may understand thereby the seeking our happiness in gratifying the imagination, (which is chiefly done by means of the eyes,) by grand, or new, or beautiful objects (if they may not all be reduced to one head; since neither grand nor beautiful objects are pleasing when the novelty of them is gone). But are not the hollowest things pleasing as long as they are new? Do not some of you, on the score of novelty, seek no small part of your happiness in that hollowest of hollows—dress? Do you not bestow more money, or (which is the same) more time or pains upon it than you did once? I doubt this is not done to please God. Then it pleases the devil. If you laid aside your needless ornaments some years ago—ruffles, necklaces, spider-caps, ugly and unbecoming bonnets,5 costly linen, expensive laces—have you not, in defiance of religion and reason, taken to them again?6

Perhaps you say you can now afford the expense. This is the quintessence of nonsense. Who gave you this addition to your fortune; or (to speak properly) lent it to you? To speak more properly still, who lodged it for a time in your hands as His stewards; informing you at the same time for what purposes He entrusted you with it? And can you afford to waste your Lord’s goods, for every part of which you are to give an account; or to expend them in any other way than that which He hath expressly appointed? Away with this vile, diabolical chant! Let it never more come out of your lips. This affording to rob God is the very chant of hell.

Do not you know that God entrusted you with that money (all that is above what buys necessaries for your families) to feed the hungry, to clothe the naked, to help the stranger, the widow, the fatherless; and, indeed, as far as it will go, to relieve the wants of all mankind? How can you, how dare you, defraud your Lord by applying it to any other purpose? When He entrusted you with a little, did He not entrust you with it that you might lay out all that little in doing good? And when He entrusted you with more, did He not entrust you with that additional money that you might do so much the more good, as you had more ability? Had you any more right to waste a pound, a shilling, or a penny, than you had before? You have, therefore, no more right to gratify the desire of the flesh, or the desire of the eyes, now than when you were a beggar. O no! do not make so poor a return to your beneficent Lord! Rather, the more He entrusts you with, be so much the more careful to employ every mite as He hath appointed.

Employing mites as do the angels

Ye angels of God, ye servants of His that continually do His pleasure: our common Lord hath entrusted you also with talents far more precious than gold and silver so that you may minister in your various offices to the heirs of salvation. Do not you employ every mite of what you have received to the end for which it was given you? And hath He not directed us to do His will on earth, as it is done by you in heaven? Brethren, what are we doing! Let us awake! Let us arise! Let us imitate those flaming ministers! Let us employ our whole soul, body, and substance according to the will of our Lord! Let us render unto God the things that are God’s; even all we are, and all we have!

Most of those who set their hearts upon riches increase when they increase, do it indirectly, as in some of the preceding instances I related. But there are others who do this more directly, being, properly, “lovers of money.” These love it for its own sake; not only for the sake of what it procures. But this vice is very rarely found in children or young persons; but only, or chiefly, in the old—in those that have the least need of money, and the least time to enjoy it.

Might not this induce one to think that in many cases it is a penal evil; that it is a sin-punishing evil; that when a man has, for many years, hid his precious talent in the earth, God delivers him up to Satan, to punish by the inordinate love of it? Then it is that he is more and more tormented by that “that execrable hunger after gold” which can never be satisfied. No, it is most true, as the very heathen observes: “As money, so the love of money grows; it increases in the same proportion.” As in a dropsy; the more you drink, the more you thirst, till that unquenchable thirst plunges you into the fire which shall never be quenched!

“But is there no way,” you may ask, “either to prevent or to cure this dire disease?” There is one preventative of it, which is also a remedy for it; and I believe there is no other under heaven. It is this. After you have gained (with the cautions above given) all you can, and saved all you can, wanting for nothing; spend not one pound, one shilling, or one penny to gratify either the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, or the pride of life; or indeed, for any other end than to please and glorify God. Having avoided this rock on the right hand, beware of that on the left. Secondly. Hoard nothing. Lay up no treasure on earth, but give all you can; that is, all you have. I defy all the men upon earth, yea, all the angels in heaven, to find any other way of extracting the poison from riches.

Wesley’s last advice

Let me add one word more. After having served you between sixty and seventy years; with dim eyes, shaking hands, and tottering feet, I give you one more advice before I sink into the dust. Mark those words of St. Paul: “Those that desire” or endeavour “to be rich,” that moment “fall into temptation.” Yea, a deep gulf of temptation, out of which nothing less than almighty power can deliver them. “They fall into a snare”—the word properly means a steel trap, which instantly crushes the animal taken therein to pieces—“and into divers foolish and hurtful desires, which plunge men into destruction and perdition.” You, above all men, who now prosper in the world, never forget these awful words! How unspeakably slippery is your path! How dangerous every step! The Lord God enable you to see your danger, and make you deeply sensible of it! O may you “awake up after His likeness, and be satisfied with it!”

Permit me to come a little closer still. Perhaps I may not trouble you any more on this subject. I am pained for you that are “rich in this world.” Do you give all you can? You who receive £500 a year, and spend only £200, do you give £300 back to God? If not, you certainly rob God of that £300. You that receive £200, and spend but £100, do you give God the £100? If not, you rob Him of just so much.

Excuses

“Nay, may I not do what I will with my own?” Here lies the ground of your mistake. It is not your own. It cannot be, unless you are Lord of heaven and earth.

“However, I must provide for my children.” Certainly. But how? By making them rich? Then you will probably make them heathens, as some of you have done already.

“What shall I do, then?” Lord, speak to their hearts, or else the preacher speaks in vain! Leave them enough to live on, not in idleness and luxury, but by honest industry. And if you have not children, upon what scriptural or rational principle can you leave a groat behind you more than will bury you? I pray consider, what are you the better for what you leave behind you? What does it signify, whether you leave behind you £10,000, or 10,000 shoes and boots?

O leave nothing behind you! Send all you have before you into a better world! Lend it, lend it all unto the Lord, and it shall be paid you again! Is there any danger that His truth should fail? It is fixed as the pillars of heaven. Haste, haste, my brethren, haste—lest you be called away before you settled what you have on this security! When this is done, you may boldly say, “Now I have nothing to do but to die! Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit! Come, Lord Jesus! Come quickly!” ~

1 £ is the symbol for the British pound. Money values are somewhat difficult to determine across the centuries and cultures. But to give a general idea, a common laborer in England in 1780 may have earned £2-3/month. This would be comparable to making approx. $300-400/month in the US economy today.

2 As mentioned in the previous footnote, the average wage for a common laborer of that time was probably in the £30/year range.

3 Approxiamately £1.

4 Wesley’s mention of a tithe here can seem to be that he is only encouraging to give a regular tithe. But notice that the context is of “reinvestment.” Many feel that they should reinvest profits so that they can then earn more, and hence have more to give later. Wesley doubts such “wisdom” and encourages a minimum of 10% to be given to the poor immediately rather than reinvested. The idea of reinvesting profits so as to have more to give later is loaded with temptation. Many seem to never get past reinvesting, and instead of giving more later they just reinvest again ... and again ... and again. And the money never does make it to the poor.

5 Without a doubt Wesley is speaking of a certain stylish bonnet that he felt was ugly, not bonnets in general.

6 Wesley never does get around, in this message, to expounding the third aspect, “the pride of life.”

Mali zikiongezeka, usiweke moyo wako juu yake. Zab. 62:10.

Utangulizi

Alikuwa na umri wa miaka 87, na alijihisi (kama alivyoandika mwenyewe) kuwa kama mtu “mwenye macho hafifu, mikono inayotetemeka, na miguu inayoyumba.” Lakini bado alikuwa na ujumbe wa kutoa. Kwa bidii inayoonekana kuwa kubwa hata kuliko ari yake ya kawaida, John Wesley aliwaonya watu wake kuhusu hatari kubwa—utajiri. Kutoka kikundi kidogo, vuguvugu lake lilikuwa limekua na kufikia wanachama 135,000 pamoja na wahubiri wa kuzunguka zaidi ya 500. Mahubiri yake yalikuwa na matokeo ya kubadili kwa dhahiri hali ya maadili na mwenendo nchini Uingereza, kiasi cha kupewa sifa ya kuiokoa Uingereza na umwagaji damu kama ule uliofuata baadaye katika Mapinduzi ya Ufaransa. Lakini uovu wa kutisha ulijificha miongoni mwa watu wake, na Wesley alitumia baadhi ya nguvu zake za mwisho kuiita uovu huo kwa jina lake.

Sisi ambao ni matajiri mara nyingi zaidi kuliko watu wa siku za John Wesley, na tuwe na masikio ya kusikia.

(Kumbuka kwamba baadhi ya Kiingereza cha Wesley kimesasishwa na kwamba vichwa vidogo si vya awali. Sahihi iliyo chini ya kichwa ni nakala ya sahihi yake mwenyewe.)

Kutokana na tamko hilo la wazi la Bwana wetu, “Ni rahisi ngamia kupita katika tundu la sindano kuliko tajiri kuingia katika ufalme wa mbinguni,” tunaweza kujifunza kwa urahisi kwamba hakuna awezaye kuwa na utajiri bila kuwa katika hatari kubwa kwa sababu yake. Lakini ikiwa hatari ya kuwa nao tu ni kubwa kiasi hicho, hatari ya kuongeza utajiri ni kubwa zaidi kiasi gani! Hatari hii ni kubwa hata kwa wale wanaopokea kile walichorithi kutoka kwa mababu zao; lakini ni kubwa zaidi sana kwa wale wanaoupata kwa ustadi na bidii yao. Kwa hiyo, hakuna jambo lenye busara zaidi kuliko tahadhari hii: “Mali zikiongezeka, usiweke moyo wako juu yake.” Zab. 62:10

Ni kweli kwamba utajiri, na kuongezeka kwake, ni zawadi ya Mungu. Hata hivyo, ni lazima kuchukua tahadhari kubwa ili kile kilichokusudiwa kuwa baraka kisigeuke kuwa laana. Ili kuzuia hili, inafaa sana kufikiria kwa uzito:

  1. Utajiri unamaanisha nini; na ni wakati gani tunaweza kusema unaongezeka.
  2. Ni nini kinachomaanishwa na kuweka mioyo yetu juu yake; na tunawezaje kuepuka kufanya hivyo.

“Utajiri” unamaanisha nini?

Kwanza, fikiria kile kinachomaanishwa hapa kwa utajiri. Kwa hakika, huenda wengine wakadhani kwamba ni vigumu sana kukosea maana ya neno hili la kawaida. Hata hivyo, kwa kweli, kuna maelfu wanaokosea kuhusu maana hiyo; na wengi wao bila kukusudia kabisa. Mtu mmoja mashuhuri, aliposikia mahubiri juu ya mada hii miaka kadhaa iliyopita, alishangaa na kukasirika, kisha akasema kwa sauti, “Kwa nini anazungumzia utajiri hapa? Hakuna tajiri Whitehaven isipokuwa Sir James L----r.”

Na ni kweli kwamba hakuna mwingine isipokuwa yeye aliyekuwa na £40,0001 kwa mwaka, na mamilioni kadhaa ya pesa taslimu. Lakini mtu anaweza kuwa tajiri hata kama hana £100 kwa mwaka, wala hata £1000 taslimu. Yeyote aliye na chakula cha kula, na nguo za kuvaa, pamoja na ziada fulani, ni tajiri. Yeyote aliye na mahitaji na starehe za maisha kwa ajili yake mwenyewe na familia yake, na kiasi kidogo cha kuwapa wale wasio navyo, kwa kweli ni tajiri; isipokuwa awe bahili, mpenda pesa, mtu anayeficha akiba ya kile anachoweza na anachopaswa kuwapa maskini. Kwa maana kama ndivyo, bado ni maskini, ingawa ana mamilioni benki; naam, ndiye maskini zaidi ya watu wote; kwa maana:

Maskini hulalamikia tu fungu la kawaida;
Tajiri aliye maskini ni maskini hasa.

Jihadhari na kutoa hukumu

Hata hivyo, hapa kunaweza kuwa na kighairi. Mtu anaweza kuwa na zaidi ya mahitaji na starehe za familia yake, na bado asiwe tajiri. Kwa maana huenda akawa na madeni; na madeni yake yanaweza kuzidi thamani ya mali yake. Lakini ikiwa ndivyo ilivyo, yeye si tajiri, hata kama ana pesa nyingi kiasi gani mikononi mwake. Naam, mfanyabiashara anaweza kuhofu kwamba hii ndiyo hali halisi ya mambo yake, iwe ni kweli au la; na hapo hawezi kutoa kwa ukarimu kama anavyotaka, kwa kuogopa kutenda bila haki. Ni watu wangapi wanaojishughulisha na biashara walio katika hali hii hasa! Hasa wale wanaofanya biashara kwa kiwango kikubwa sana; kwa maana mara nyingi mambo yao yamechanganyika kiasi kwamba haiwezekani kubaini kwa usahihi ni kiasi gani wanachomiliki, au hata kama wana thamani yoyote au hawana. Je, hatupaswi kuwaachia nafasi ya kuzingatia hali hiyo?

Na jihadhari kutoa hukumu ya haraka kuhusu mali za wengine. Huenda kukawa na siri katika hali ya mtu ambazo ni wachache tu, mbali na Mungu, wanaozijua. Miaka kadhaa iliyopita nilimwambia bwana mmoja, “Bwana, nina hofu kwamba wewe ni mchoyo.”

Akaniuliza, “Una sababu gani ya kuwa na hofu hiyo?”

Nikamjibu, “Mwaka mmoja uliopita, nilipokusanya michango kwa ajili ya gharama za kukarabati Foundery, ulitoa guineas tano. Katika mchango wa mwaka huu ulitoa nusu guinea tu.”

Hakujibu; lakini baada ya muda akaniuliza, “Tafadhali, bwana, nijibu swali moja: Kwa nini unaishi kwa kula viazi?” (Nilifanya hivyo kwa miaka kati ya mitatu na minne.)

Nikamjibu, “Kumesaidia sana afya yangu.”

Akajibu, “Naamini hivyo. Lakini je, hukufanya hivyo pia ili kuokoa pesa?”

Nikasema, “Ndiyo; kwa maana kile ninachookoa kwenye gharama ya chakula changu mwenyewe kinamlisha mtu mwingine ambaye la sivyo hangekuwa na chakula.”

“Lakini, bwana,” akasema, “ikiwa hiyo ndiyo sababu yako, unaweza kuokoa zaidi sana. Namjua mtu anayeenda sokoni mwanzoni mwa kila juma: Huko hununua kiasi cha parsnip cha senti moja, ambacho hukichemsha katika maji mengi. Parsnip humfaa kama chakula, na maji hunywa kwa juma lote linalofuata. Kwa hiyo chakula na kinywaji chake vyote kwa pamoja humgharimu senti moja tu kwa juma.”

Alifanya hivyo daima, ingawa wakati huo alipata £200 kwa mwaka,2 ili aweze kulipa madeni aliyokuwa ameingia kabla hajamjua Mungu! Na huyu ndiye niliyemhesabu kuwa mtu mchoyo!

Vipi kuhusu wewe?

Hata hivyo, kuna watu wanaojua mbele za Mungu kwamba wao ni matajiri. Na bila shaka baadhi ya ninyi ni miongoni mwao. Mna mali nyingi zaidi za dunia hii kuliko zinavyohitajika kwa ajili yenu wenyewe au familia zenu. Kila mtu na ajitathmini mwenyewe. Je, mali zenu zinaongezeka? Je, hamlielewi tamko hili lililo wazi? Je, hamna pesa nyingi zaidi, au mali nyingi zaidi zenye thamani ya pesa, kuliko mlizokuwa nazo miaka 10 au 20 iliyopita, au wakati kama huu mwaka uliopita? Ikiwa mnaweka hesabu, mnaweza kujua hili kwa urahisi. Kwa kweli, mnapaswa kujua; la sivyo, hata katika jambo hili hamfanyi kazi vizuri kama mawakili wa mamoni ya udhalimu. Na kila mtu, awe mfanyabiashara au la, anapaswa kujua kama mali zake zinapungua au zinaongezeka.

Hata hivyo, wengi wamegundua njia ya kutopata utajiri kamwe, hata kama mali zao zinaongezeka kiasi gani. Hivi ndivyo wanavyofanya: Pesa zinapoingia, wanaziwekeza mara moja, ama katika ardhi au katika kupanua biashara yao. Kwa njia hii, kila mmoja wao, kwa kuweka akiba ya pesa taslimu chini, bado anaweza kusema, “Mimi si tajiri.” Anaweza kusema hivyo hata kama ana mali mara 10, 20, au 100 zaidi ya alivyokuwa nazo miaka kadhaa iliyopita.

Jambo hili linaweza kuelezwa kwa kisa cha hivi karibuni: Miaka michache iliyopita, bwana mmoja alimwendea mfanyabiashara jijini London na kumwambia, “Bwana, naomba unipe guinea3 moja kwa ajili ya familia yenye sifa nzuri iliyo katika dhiki kubwa.”

Akajibu, “Kwa kweli, Bw. M., siwezi kumudu kukupa sasa hivi; lakini ukija kuniona nitakapokuwa na thamani ya £10,000, nitakupa guineas kumi.”

Baada ya muda, Bw. M. alimwendea tena na kusema, “Bwana, nakudai utimize ahadi yako; sasa una thamani ya £10,000.”

Akajibu, “Hilo ni kweli kabisa: Lakini nakuhakikishia, sasa siwezi kutoa guinea moja kwa urahisi kama nilivyoweza wakati ule.”

Mtu anaweza kujidanganya kwa hila hii ya werevu. Na anaweza kuwadanganya watu wengine; kwa maana mradi tu “unajitendea mema, watu watakusifu.” “Ni mtu mwema hasa,” asema mkazi wa London, “ana thamani ya plum moja” (£100,000). Lakini, ole wake! Hawezi kumdanganya Mungu; na hawezi kumdanganya Ibilisi. La hasha! Laana ya Mungu iko juu yako tayari, na juu ya vyote ulivyo navyo. Na kesho, Ibilisi atakapoitwaa roho yako, je, hatasema, “Utajiri wako wote utakufaa nini?” Je, utanunua mto wa kulaza kichwa chako katika ziwa la moto uwakao kwa kiberiti? Au utakupatia kikombe cha “maji ya kuupoza ulimi wako,” huku ukiteswa katika mwali huo?” Fuata kwa makini maelekezo ya hekima yaliyotolewa hapa ili Mungu asikuambie, “Mpumbavu wewe!”

Kwa hiyo, ujanja huu wa akili hautakusaidia. Hautakulinda dhidi ya ghadhabu ya Mungu wala uovu na nguvu za Ibilisi. Tayari umetiwa hatiani kwa “kuuweka moyo wako” juu ya mali zako ikiwa unawekeza tena kila kitu ulicho nacho kilicho zaidi ya mahitaji ya maisha, ili kuongeza pesa juu ya pesa, nyumba juu ya nyumba, au shamba juu ya shamba, bila kuwapa maskini angalau sehemu ya kumi ya mapato yako (kiasi kinachotolewa na Wayahudi). Kwa njia yoyote ile mali zako ziwe zimeongezeka, iwe kwa kazi au bila kazi; iwe kwa biashara, urithi, au njia nyingine yoyote; isipokuwa michango yako ya hisani iongezeke kwa uwiano huo huo; isipokuwa utoe sehemu kamili ya kumi ya mali zako, ya mapato yako ya kudumu na ya mara kwa mara; bila shaka umeuweka moyo wako juu ya dhahabu yako, nayo “itakula nyama yako kama moto!”4

Ugumu wa moyo wa uchoyo

Lo! Nani awezaye kumshawishi tajiri kwamba ameweka moyo wake juu ya utajiri? Kwa zaidi ya nusu karne nimezungumza juu ya jambo hili kwa uwazi wote nilioweza. Lakini matokeo yake yamekuwa madogo kiasi gani! Nina shaka kama katika muda huo wote nimewahi kuwashawishi watu hamsini wachoyo kwamba wana uchoyo. Mpenda pesa alipoelezewa kwa uwazi kabisa, na kuchorwa kwa rangi kali zaidi, ni nani aliyejihusisha na maelezo hayo? Ni nani ambaye Mungu, na wote waliomjua, walimwambia, “Wewe ndiye huyo mtu!” Mungu akisema na yeyote miongoni mwenu mlio hapa, Lo, msizibe masikio yenu! Badala yake, semeni pamoja na Zakayo, “Tazama, Bwana, natoa nusu ya mali yangu kwa maskini; na ikiwa nimemdhulumu mtu yeyote kwa jambo lolote, namrudishia mara nne.” Hakuwa na maana kwamba alikuwa amefanya hivyo zamani; bali alikusudia kufanya hivyo kuanzia wakati huo na kuendelea. Nakuagiza mbele za Mungu, wewe mpenda pesa, “nenda ukafanye vivyo hivyo!”

Nina ujumbe kutoka kwa Mungu kwa ajili yako, ewe tajiri! Iwe utasikia au hutaki kusikia. Utajiri umeongezeka kwako; kwa kuhatarisha roho yako, “usiweke moyo wako juu yake!” Mshukuru Yeye aliyekupa talanta hiyo, uwezo mkubwa wa kutenda mema. Hata hivyo, usithubutu kuufurahia isipokuwa kwa hofu na kutetemeka, “Jihadhari usiushikamane nao, usije ukanaswa na kuangamia.” Usiufanye kuwa lengo lako, furaha yako kuu, furaha yako, mungu wako! Hakikisha kwamba hutarajii furaha kutokana na pesa, wala kutokana na kitu chochote kinachoweza kununuliwa kwa pesa; katika kutosheleza tamaa ya mwili, au tamaa ya macho, au kiburi cha uzima.

Lakini na tuzingatie mambo mahususi; na kila mmoja wenu aangalie kwa uaminifu nafsi yake mwenyewe. Ikiwa yeyote miongoni mwenu sasa ana mali mara mbili, tatu, au nne ya ile aliyokuwa nayo aliponiona mara ya kwanza, na ajichunguze kwa uaminifu aone kama ameuweka moyo wake, si moja kwa moja juu ya pesa au utajiri wenyewe, basi juu ya baadhi ya vitu vinavyoweza kununuliwa kwa pesa; jambo ambalo ni sawa na hilo. Mtume Yohana anaviweka vyote chini ya jina hilo la jumla, ulimwengu; na tamaa yake, au kutafuta furaha ndani yake, chini ya msemo huu, “kuupenda ulimwengu.”

Kufafanua “ulimwengu”

Anaugawa katika matawi matatu, “tamaa ya mwili, tamaa ya macho, na kiburi cha uzima.” Jichunguzeni kwa haki kuhusu mambo haya.

  • Kwanza, kuhusu “tamaa ya mwili.” Ninaamini hii inamaanisha kutafuta furaha katika vitu vinavyoridhisha hisi. Kwa kutoa mfano mmoja: Je, hamtafuti furaha yenu katika kuongeza raha ya kuonja? Kwa kusema wazi zaidi: Je, hamli chakula kingi zaidi, au kilicho kitamu zaidi, kuliko mlivyokula miaka kumi au ishirini iliyopita? Je, hamnywi vinywaji vingi zaidi, au vinywaji vya gharama zaidi, kuliko mlivyokuwa mkifanya wakati huo? Je, bado mnalala kwenye kitanda kigumu kama mlivyokuwa mkilala zamani, ikiwa afya yenu inaruhusu? Kugusia jambo moja zaidi: Je, mnafunga mara nyingi kama mlivyokuwa mkifunga mlipokuwa maskini, sasa kwa kuwa mmetajirika? Kwa kila sababu, je, hamkupaswa kufanya hivyo mara nyingi zaidi badala ya mara chache zaidi? Ninaogopa kwamba mioyo yenu wenyewe inawahukumu. Hamko safi katika jambo hili.
  • Tawi la pili la kuupenda ulimwengu, “tamaa ya macho,” lina wigo mpana zaidi. Tunaweza kuelewa kwa hilo kutafuta furaha katika kuridhisha mawazo (ambako hasa hufanywa kupitia macho), kwa vitu vya fahari, au vipya, au vizuri (ikiwa vyote haviwezi kuingizwa katika kundi moja; kwa kuwa vitu vya fahari wala vizuri havipendezi tena baada ya kupoteza upekee wake). Lakini, je, vitu visivyo na maana kabisa havipendezi mradi tu ni vipya? Je, baadhi yenu, kwa sababu ya upekee wake, hamtafuti sehemu kubwa ya furaha yenu katika kitu hicho kisicho na maana kuliko vyote—mavazi? Je, hamtumii pesa nyingi zaidi, au (ambayo ni sawa) muda au juhudi nyingi zaidi kuyashughulikia kuliko zamani? Nina shaka kwamba mnafanya hivyo ili kumpendeza Mungu. Basi, mnamfurahisha Ibilisi. Ikiwa miaka kadhaa iliyopita mliacha mapambo yenu yasiyo ya lazima—mikunjo ya mapambo, mikufu, kofia za wavu wa buibui, kofia za wanawake mbaya na zisizowapendeza,5 kitani cha gharama, kamba za mapambo za bei ghali—je, hamkuyarudia tena, kwa ukaidi mkipuuza dini na akili?6

Labda mnasema kwamba sasa mna uwezo wa kumudu gharama hiyo. Huu ni upuuzi mtupu kabisa. Ni nani aliyekupa ongezeko hili la mali; au (kusema kwa usahihi) aliyolikopesha? Au kusema kwa usahihi zaidi, ni nani aliyeliweka kwa muda mikononi mwako kama wakili Wake; huku akikujulisha wakati huohuo madhumuni aliyokukabidhi mali hiyo? Je, unaweza kumudu kupoteza mali ya Bwana wako, ambayo utapaswa kutoa hesabu ya kila sehemu yake; au kuitumia kwa njia nyingine yoyote isipokuwa ile aliyoagiza waziwazi? Ondokeni na wimbo huu mwovu, wa kishetani! Usitoke tena midomoni mwenu. “Kumudu” kumwibia Mungu ndilo hasa wimbo wa jehanamu.

Hamjui kwamba Mungu aliwakabidhi pesa hizo (zote zilizozidi zile zinazohitajika kununua mahitaji ya familia zenu) ili kuwalisha wenye njaa, kuwavika walio uchi, kuwasaidia wageni, wajane, yatima; na kwa kweli, kadiri zinavyotosha, kutimiza mahitaji ya wanadamu wote? Mnawezaje, mnathubutuje, kumsaliti Bwana wenu kwa kuzitumia kwa kusudi jingine lolote? Alipowakabidhi kiasi kidogo, je, hakukikabidhi ili mtumie kiasi hicho chote kutenda mema? Na alipowakabidhi zaidi, je, hakuwakabidhi pesa hizo za ziada ili mtende mema mengi zaidi, kwa kuwa mlikuwa na uwezo mkubwa zaidi? Je, mlikuwa na haki zaidi ya kupoteza pauni moja, shilingi moja, au senti moja kuliko mlivyokuwa nayo hapo awali? Kwa hiyo, hamna haki zaidi ya kutosheleza tamaa ya mwili au tamaa ya macho sasa kuliko mlivyokuwa nayo mlipokuwa ombaomba. La hasha! Msimlipe Bwana wenu mwema kwa malipo duni hivyo! Badala yake, kadiri anavyowakabidhi zaidi, muwe waangalifu zaidi kutumia kila senti kama alivyoagiza.

Kutumia kila senti kama malaika wafanyavyo

Ninyi malaika wa Mungu, watumishi Wake ambao hutimiza mapenzi Yake daima: Bwana wetu wa wote amewakabidhi ninyi pia talanta zilizo za thamani zaidi sana kuliko dhahabu na fedha ili muwahudumie warithi wa wokovu katika nyadhifa zenu mbalimbali. Je, hamtumii kila senti ya kile mlichopokea kwa kusudi lilelile mlilopewa? Na je, hakutuagiza sisi tutimize mapenzi Yake duniani kama yanavyotimizwa nanyi mbinguni? Ndugu, tunafanya nini! Na tuamke! Na tusimame! Na tuwaige wahudumu hao wawakao! Na tutumie nafsi, mwili na mali zetu zote kulingana na mapenzi ya Bwana wetu! Na tumpe Mungu vitu vilivyo vya Mungu; yaani, vyote tulivyo na vyote tulivyo navyo!

Wengi wa wale wanaoweka mioyo yao juu ya utajiri hufanya hivyo kwa njia isiyo ya moja kwa moja utajiri wao unapoongezeka, kama katika baadhi ya mifano iliyotajwa hapo awali. Lakini kuna wengine wanaofanya hivyo moja kwa moja zaidi, na kwa kweli ni “wapenda pesa.” Wanazipenda pesa kwa ajili ya pesa zenyewe; si kwa sababu tu ya kile zinachonunua. Lakini uovu huu haupatikani sana kwa watoto au vijana; unapatikana tu, au hasa, kwa wazee—wale ambao hawana uhitaji mkubwa zaidi wa pesa, na wana muda mchache zaidi wa kuzifurahia.

Je, jambo hili halingeweza kumfanya mtu afikiri kwamba katika visa vingi ni uovu wa adhabu; uovu unaoadhibu dhambi; kwamba mtu anapokuwa ameficha talanta yake ya thamani ardhini kwa miaka mingi, Mungu humtia mikononi mwa Shetani ili aadhibiwe kwa kuipenda kupita kiasi? Ndipo anapoteswa zaidi na zaidi na “tamaa hiyo ya kuchukiza ya dhahabu” isiyoweza kutoshelezwa kamwe. Naam, ni kweli kabisa, kama hata mpagani mwenyewe anavyoona: “Kama pesa zinavyoongezeka, ndivyo upendo wa pesa unavyoongezeka; huongezeka kwa uwiano huo huo.” Ni kama ugonjwa wa kuvimba mwili kwa maji; kadiri unavyokunywa, ndivyo kiu yako inavyozidi, mpaka kiu hiyo isiyozimika inakuingiza katika moto usiozimwa kamwe!

“Lakini hakuna njia,” huenda ukauliza, “ya kuzuia au kutibu ugonjwa huu wa kutisha?” Kuna njia moja ya kuuzuia, ambayo pia ni tiba yake; na ninaamini hakuna nyingine chini ya mbingu. Hii ndiyo: Baada ya kupata (kwa kufuata tahadhari zilizotolewa hapo juu) kila kitu unachoweza, na kuokoa kila kitu unachoweza, bila kukosa chochote, usitumie pauni moja, shilingi moja, wala senti moja kutosheleza tamaa ya mwili, tamaa ya macho, au kiburi cha uzima; wala kwa kusudi jingine lolote isipokuwa kumpendeza na kumtukuza Mungu. Baada ya kuepuka mwamba huu ulio upande wa kulia, jihadhari na ule ulio upande wa kushoto. Pili. Usihodhi chochote. Usiweke hazina duniani, bali toa kila kitu unachoweza; yaani, kila ulicho nacho. Natoa changamoto kwa watu wote duniani, naam, kwa malaika wote mbinguni, watafute njia nyingine yoyote ya kuondoa sumu katika utajiri.

Ushauri wa mwisho wa Wesley

Niongeze neno moja zaidi. Baada ya kuwahudumia kwa miaka kati ya sitini na sabini; nikiwa na macho hafifu, mikono inayotetemeka, na miguu inayoyumba, nawapa ushauri mmoja zaidi kabla sijazama mavumbini. Zingatieni maneno hayo ya Mtakatifu Paulo: “Wale wanaotamani” au kujitahidi “kuwa matajiri,” wakati huohuo “huanguka katika majaribu.” Naam, huanguka katika shimo refu la majaribu, ambalo hakuna kitu kingine isipokuwa nguvu za Mwenyezi Mungu kinachoweza kuwaokoa. “Wanaanguka katika mtego”—neno hilo lina maana ya mtego wa chuma, ambao humponda mara moja mnyama anayenaswa humo vipandevipande—“na katika tamaa nyingi zisizo na akili na zenye kudhuru, ambazo huwazamisha watu katika maangamizi na upotevu.” Ninyi, kuliko watu wote, ambao sasa mnafanikiwa duniani, msisahau kamwe maneno haya ya kutisha! Njia yenu ina utelezi kiasi gani usioelezeka! Kila hatua ina hatari kiasi gani! Bwana Mungu na awawezeshe kuona hatari yenu, na awafanye muielewe kwa undani! Laiti “mngeamka katika mfano Wake, na kuridhika nao!”

Niruhusuni niwasogelee zaidi kidogo. Huenda nisihangaike tena nanyi kuhusu mada hii. Nina huzuni kwa ajili yenu “mlio matajiri katika ulimwengu huu.” Je, mnatoa kila kitu mnachoweza? Ninyi mnaopokea £500 kwa mwaka, na kutumia £200 tu, je, mnampa Mungu £300? Kama sivyo, kwa hakika mnammuibia Mungu £300 hizo. Ninyi mnaopokea £200 na kutumia £100 tu, je, mnampa Mungu £100 hizo? Kama sivyo, mnammuibia kiasi hicho.

Visingizio

“Je, siwezi kufanya nitakavyo na mali yangu mwenyewe?” Hapa ndipo msingi wa kosa lenu ulipo. Si mali yenu. Haiwezi kuwa yenu, isipokuwa muwe Bwana wa mbingu na dunia.

“Hata hivyo, ni lazima niwaandalie watoto wangu mahitaji.” Bila shaka. Lakini kwa njia gani? Kwa kuwafanya wawe matajiri? Basi huenda mtawafanya kuwa wapagani, kama baadhi yenu mlivyokwisha kufanya.

“Basi, nifanye nini?” Bwana, nena na mioyo yao, la sivyo mhubiri anazungumza bure! Waachieni kiasi cha kutosha kuishi, si kwa uvivu na anasa, bali kwa kufanya kazi kwa uaminifu. Na ikiwa hamna watoto, ni kanuni gani ya Kimaandiko au ya kimantiki inayoweza kuhalalisha kuwaachia zaidi ya senti moja baada ya kufa, isipokuwa tu kiasi cha gharama ya mazishi yenu? Tafadhali fikirini, mnanufaikaje na kile mnachoacha nyuma? Kuna tofauti gani kama mnaacha £10,000 au jozi 10,000 za viatu na buti?

Lo, msiache chochote nyuma yenu! Tuma kila ulicho nacho mbele yako katika ulimwengu ulio bora! Kikopesheni, kikopesheni chote kwa Bwana, naye atawalipa! Je, kuna hatari yoyote kwamba ukweli Wake utashindwa? Umeimarishwa kama nguzo za mbingu. Harakeni, harakeni, ndugu zangu, harakeni—msije mkaitwa kuondoka kabla hamjaweka mali zenu kwenye dhamana hii! Hili likishafanyika, mnaweza kusema kwa ujasiri, “Sasa sina la kufanya ila kufa! Baba, mikononi mwako naiweka roho yangu! Njoo, Bwana Yesu! Njoo upesi!” ~

1 £ ni alama ya pauni ya Uingereza. Ni vigumu kiasi kuamua thamani za pesa katika nyakati na tamaduni tofauti. Lakini ili kutoa wazo la jumla, huenda mfanyakazi wa kawaida nchini Uingereza mwaka 1780 alipata £2-3 kwa mwezi. Hii ingelingana na kupata takriban $300-400 kwa mwezi katika uchumi wa Marekani wa leo.

2 Kama ilivyotajwa katika tanbihi iliyotangulia, huenda mshahara wa wastani wa mfanyakazi wa kawaida wakati huo ulikuwa karibu £30 kwa mwaka.

3 Takriban £1.

4 Kutajwa kwa zaka na Wesley hapa kunaweza kuonekana kana kwamba anahimiza tu kutoa zaka ya kawaida. Lakini kumbuka kwamba muktadha ni “kuwekeza tena.” Wengi huhisi kwamba wanapaswa kuwekeza tena faida ili wapate mapato zaidi na, kwa hiyo, wawe na zaidi ya kutoa baadaye. Wesley ana shaka na “hekima” hiyo na anahimiza kutoa maskini angalau asilimia 10 mara moja badala ya kuwekeza tena. Wazo la kuwekeza tena faida ili kuwa na zaidi ya kutoa baadaye limejaa majaribu. Wengi wanaonekana kutofika hatua ya kutoa kwa sababu wanaendelea kuwekeza tena, na badala ya kutoa zaidi baadaye, wanawekeza tena ... na tena ... na tena. Na pesa hizo haziwafikii kamwe maskini.

5 Bila shaka yoyote, Wesley anazungumzia kofia fulani ya mtindo aliyoiona kuwa mbaya, si kofia zote kwa ujumla.

6 Katika ujumbe huu Wesley hakuwahi kupata nafasi ya kufafanua kipengele cha tatu, “kiburi cha uzima.”
